title: Make do

brief.story: The LED needs about 350 Ω, but the drawer only has 100 Ω, 470 Ω and 1 kΩ resistors left. It’s Sunday and the shop is shut.
brief.goal: Combine resistors from the drawer so LED1 carries 18–23 mA.

hints: You need about 7 V ÷ 20 mA = 350 Ω between column 3 and LED1 (column 14). No single drawer value is close.
Side by side (parallel), two resistors give less than the smaller one: both from column 3 to column 14.
470 Ω and 1 kΩ in parallel make 320 Ω: 21.9 mA. Three 1 kΩ in parallel (333 Ω) work too.

spec.explain: In series resistances add; in parallel the total is less than the smallest: 470 Ω ∥ 1 kΩ = 320 Ω.

debrief: Series adds resistances, parallel divides them: 470 Ω ∥ 1 kΩ = 470 × 1000 ÷ 1470 = 320 Ω. Repair techs do this all the time when the exact value isn’t in the drawer, and it’s also how you make a resistor that can take more heat: two in parallel share the power.
